title: When his father stopped playing; the two-banjo bands with Harry
summary: His father quit around World War I; Julius and a rival banjoist played opposite ends of a band with alternating solos.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: When did your daddy quit playing?
Mmm, I don't know what year. But, my daddy quit playing. Quick time.
Think about how old you were, how old were you getting that way?

It must have been around in the, World War I. My daddy wasn't old enough to go to, no, my daddy had, I think it was 18 to 45, that, in World War I, they were taken from 18 to 45. Where Cal was too young, and my daddy was about a year or two years too old. So, it was around 50, they could stop. Right, mm-hmm. And so, that made my daddy, my daddy was too old, and Cal was too young. Oh, but Cal, he was anxious to go, he wanted to get out there. He didn't know what he was going to do out there anyway, but he wanted to go. So, but, then, they had, stuff They had Harry Fagmitude, he was a bandol player. And Harry, Harry Fagmitude and I.
I think you remember these names so well.

Harry Fagmitude and I, at the 100th Vigilum, they gave a dance if they wanted to draw a big crowd. Well, they want Harry and I, they used to call two banjo players bumping at each other. You know what I mean? Well, they'd hire me on banjo and hire Howard on banjo. Well, at that end of the band, they put Howard over there. And at this end of the band, they put me over here. And Howard would take a solo over there. And on that whole number now, it wasn't like at the preservation hall, everybody would take a number. Because you can bore the people like that. You know what I mean? But on this number, like we played this time, Harry would take a solo. Then the whole band pick up the number, and they'd play their whole number, and then they'd go out. Well, they'd play another number, and then the next number they would play would be for me to take a solo. You see, because I would take one every number, Harry would take one, the banjo players would be boring each other. I mean, would be boring the people, see.
